top_signal.title: People tell me my B2B platform is a great idea, but getting them to actually use it is another story. What am I missing?
top_signal.summary: I’ve built a niche B2B platform and I’m struggling with getting users to actually USE it. Has anyone cracked this?   I launched a platform earlier this year for the UK construction/retrofit industry. The idea is to connect businesses with opportunities, jobs, training, funding and other companies in the sector.   The feedback on the concept and the platform itself has been really positive. I’ve also managed to get some fairly big industry organisations involved, I run in-person networking events alongside it and I’m constantly speaking to businesses in the sector.   The problem is activation. I can get people to sign up, but getting them to actually log in regularly, post opportunities, submit expressions of interest, connect with people etc. is proving much harder.   I’ve emailed people, personally reached out, offered to upload their first opportunity for them and tried to make it as easy as possible. People will tell me they love the idea and intend to use it, then… nothing.   It’s £20/month with a 30-day free trial. I currently have 17 paying subscribers, but recently had 11 cancellations, which has knocked my confidence quite a bit.   I know churn is part of building a subscription business and I’m still very early, but I’m conscious that simply throwing more people into the top of the funnel isn’t the answer if they aren’t becoming active users.
